title: 17 — Valdez Estate: Parents and Spouse Without Descendants

story.narrative:
Arsenio Valdez died on 18 February 2025 in Baguio City, Philippines, leaving a will executed on 12 June 2024. Arsenio left no children or other descendants. His wife Elena Valdez and legitimate parents Mateo and Lourdes Valdez survived him, as did his sister Teresa Valdez, nephew Nico Valdez and niece Celia Valdez. His original clinic beneficiary, Rosa Medina, predeceased him. Marriage, filiation, probate, capacity and ownership are stipulated, and the figures exclude any separately owned marital-property share. Gross assets are PHP 27,000,000 and total liabilities are PHP 3,000,000, with no additional debts or donations to collate.

The will confirms the parents' and spouse's unburdened legitimes. It leaves the Valdez dialysis-clinic business interest, worth PHP 5,000,000 with a PHP 1,400,000 loan, to Rosa; Nico alone substitutes upon her predecease, repudiation or incapacity and must discharge that loan from the interest. The loan is already included in total liabilities. The recipient must obtain renewed health-department accreditation and establish a subsidized dialysis program within eighteen months; Nico met both requirements and accepted. The will also leaves the PHP 2,400,000 medical-research bond portfolio to the Cordillera Kidney Foundation, subject to termination if it diverts principal to administrative salaries within five years; no diversion has occurred. Celia has no gift or substitution under this will. Compute the distribution of Arsenio Valdez's estate.
story.circumstances: The marriage, filiation, ownership, capacity, probate, and valuations are stipulated. There are no descendants, donations subject to collation, or other debts. Under Articles 889, 890, and 893, the parents collectively receive one-half, the surviving spouse one-fourth, and the remaining one-fourth is disposable. The will expressly directs the clinic recipient to discharge its identified debt from that interest. The net equity alone is charged against the free portion.

Rosa predeceased Arsenio, so Nico takes the clinic only as the named substitute, not by representation.

title: 18 — Ramos Estate: Grandparent Lines, Spouse and Illegitimate Children

story.narrative:
Celestino Ramos died on 22 March 2025 in Vigan City, Philippines, leaving a will executed on 8 August 2024. Celestino left no legitimate descendants. His legitimate parents Rogelio Ramos and Adela Cruz and maternal grandfather Gabino Cruz predeceased him. His paternal grandparents Eusebio and Felisa Ramos, maternal grandmother Helena Cruz, wife Maribel Ramos, and acknowledged illegitimate children Paolo and Regina Ramos survived. The three surviving grandparents are equally near in degree. Marriage, filiation, ownership, capacity and will formalities are stipulated. Gross assets are PHP 44,000,000 and total liabilities are PHP 4,000,000, with no additional debts or donations to collate.

The will recognizes the compulsory shares and leaves a PHP 3,000,000 deposit legacy to Tomas Uy. Ursula Uy and Victor Uy substitute upon his predecease, repudiation or incapacity in fixed shares of 2:1, and reciprocally substitute for each other if either cannot take. Tomas validly repudiated; both substitutes accepted, so the further fallback has not occurred. The deposit's gross value is PHP 3,600,000 less a PHP 600,000 secured pledge already included in total liabilities; the stated legacy is its net amount. The will also leaves the movable art archive, worth PHP 2,000,000, to Wilma Ramos with an express duty to preserve it and transmit it to her child Xavier Ramos at her death. Wilma and Xavier were alive and capable at Celestino's death, and Wilma remains alive at the accounting date. Compute the distribution of Celestino Ramos's estate.
story.circumstances: The grandparents are of equal degree. Filiation, recognition, marriage, ownership, capacity, and will formalities are stipulated. Under Articles 890 and 899, ascendants receive one-half, illegitimate children one-fourth, the spouse one-eighth, and only one-eighth remains free.

Paolo and Regina divide the illegitimate children's collective quarter equally.
The voluntary gifts are confined to the PHP 5,000,000 free eighth.

title: 19 — Soriano Estate: Two Legitimate and Five Illegitimate Children

story.narrative:
Damian Soriano died on 30 April 2025 in Davao City, Philippines, leaving a will executed on 20 September 2024. Damian was survived by his wife Sofia Soriano; their legitimate children Andres and Beatriz Soriano; and five duly proved illegitimate children, Carlo Reyes, Dina Reyes, Emilio Cruz, Flora Cruz and Gregorio Lim. All seven filiations, the marriage, estate ownership and probate are stipulated. Gross assets are PHP 54,000,000 and total liabilities are PHP 6,000,000, with no additional debts or donations to collate.

The will confirms the compulsory heirs' legitimes and additionally leaves the resort business interest, with PHP 8,000,000 net value after its PHP 2,000,000 development loan, and a separate PHP 2,000,000 cash legacy to Helena Ong. The loan is included in total liabilities. Both gifts require Helena and Julia Ong jointly to restore the mangrove reserve. Ismael Ong alone is named as substitute for Helena upon predecease, repudiation or incapacity in either gift; Julia is a participant in the restoration requirement, not a separate legatee. The resort legacy would terminate if its holder converted the protected mangrove land into private villas within ten years. Determine the effect of the compulsory shares on these proposed gifts before addressing any conditional entitlement. Compute the distribution of Damian Soriano's estate.
story.circumstances: All seven filiations, the marriage, ownership, and probate facts are stipulated. The exercise applies Articles 888, 895, and 897: legitimate children first receive their collective half; the spouse receives one legitimate-child share; illegitimate children receive the balance available for their legitimes, subject to the statutory cap.

No disposable portion remains, so every outside legacy or legacy is fully reduced.

story.narrative:
Eloisa Bautista died on 1 February 2026 in Manila, Philippines, leaving a will executed on 1 June 2025. Eloisa was the legitimate child of Alberto Bautista and Remedios Santos and died unmarried and without descendants. Both parents survived, together with paternal grandfather Benigno Bautista and maternal grandmother Leonora Santos. Paternal grandmother Concepcion Bautista died in 2024. All assets were self-acquired; filiation, probate, capacity and acceptance are stipulated, except for the stated predecease. The accounting date is 30 June 2026. Gross assets are PHP 26,000,000 and total liabilities are PHP 2,000,000, with no additional debts or donations to collate.

The will confirms the parents' unburdened legitimes and leaves cash legacies of PHP 6,000,000 each to Concepcion and Leonora. Benigno is the named substitute for Concepcion on predecease, repudiation or incapacity. The recipient of Concepcion's gift must obtain the city archivist's approval of a family-record preservation plan, a requirement expressly binding Benigno; his plan was approved on 1 March 2026 and he accepted. Leonora's gift depends on the municipal museum opening its genealogy room by 30 June 2026; it opened on 1 April and she accepted. Compute the distribution of Eloisa Bautista's estate.
story.circumstances: Solved snapshot: 30 June 2026. No surviving spouse, children or further descendants. All filiation and stated adoption facts, probate, capacity and acceptance are stipulated; exceptions are expressly stated. No collation donations, disinheritance, unworthiness, omitted liabilities or marital-property share. All assets were self-acquired. Grandparent and parent labels describe their relationship to this testator, not their personal worth or necessarily their own birth status. Articles 887(2), 889 and 890 reserve half of this legitimate child's estate for her legitimate parents. With both parents living, divide that reserve equally. Grandparents have no compulsory allocation while the parents survive.
keyFacts: Articles 887(2), 889 and 890 reserve half of this legitimate child's estate for her legitimate parents. With both parents living, divide that reserve equally. Grandparents have no compulsory allocation while the parents survive.

Equality governs the parents' PHP 6,000,000 legitimes. Benigno and Leonora receive voluntary legacies, not a represented parental legitime. The simple substitute takes only the failed PHP 6,000,000 gift.
Only the free portion is subject to conditions or testamentary substitution (Articles 872 and 904). The guide accounts for current takers, not hypothetical substitute shares.

doctrines: Articles 887(2), 889 and 890 reserve half of this legitimate child's estate for her legitimate parents. With both parents living, divide that reserve equally. Grandparents have no compulsory allocation while the parents survive.

Equality governs the parents' PHP 6,000,000 legitimes. Benigno and Leonora receive voluntary legacies, not a represented parental legitime. The simple substitute takes only the failed PHP 6,000,000 gift.
Representation is a legal fiction, but Article 972 bars it in the ascending line. The per-stirpes rule in Article 974 does not authorize a grandparent to represent a parent.
